Anup Bagchi  
Good afternoon, and welcome to the results call of ICICI Life Insurance Limited for the 
half-year ended September 30th, 2026. I have several of my senior colleagues with me 
on this call, Sidharatha Mishra, Chief Operating Officer; Amish Banker, Chief Distribution 
Officer; Dhiren Salian, Chief Financial Officer; Judhajit Das, Chief Service Delivery; Manish 
Kumar, Chief Investment Officer; Souvik Jash, Appointed Actuary; and Dhiraj Chugha, 
Chief Investor Relations Officer. 
As you are aware, the Board has appointed Sidharatha as the MD and CEO of ICICI Life 
for a tenure of 5 years, beginning October 14, 2026, subject to the requisite approvals. 
He has already assumed the role of COO from October 6, 2026. 
As my tenure as MD and CEO comes to an end today, I want to sincerely thank each one 
of you for the trust and support you have extended to me, not just at ICICI Life, but also 
over more than three decades with the ICICI Group. 
I also extend my best wishes to my colleague, Sidharatha, and I am confident that he will 
lead the company to continued success. Thank you very much. Now over to you, 
Sidharatha. 
 
Sidharatha Mishra 
Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you, Anup. It is truly a privilege to lead ICICI Life. Having 
spent over 28 years within the ICICI Group, the group's values and DNA are deeply 
ingrained in me, shaped by experiences across diverse businesses over the years. 
ICICI Life is a resilient organisation, supported by a strong leadership team with deep 
domain expertise and a disciplined approach to steer the business. Customer-centricity 
has always been ICICI Life's core ethos, and this unwavering commitment will continue 
to guide every action we take. 
Our strategy remains unchanged, delivering sustainable VNB growth while balancing 
business growth, profitability, and risk and prudence. Protection and annuity stay central 
to our strategy, addressing significant underpenetrated needs in India. As we grow 
protection business, we will continue to focus on increasing the sum assured in a 
sustainable manner. 
Our customer-focused product suite, well-diversified distribution network, innovative 
and customer-first sales and service practices, industry-leading quality parameters, and 
strong risk and capital metrics position us well to capture emerging opportunities. 
I am stepping into this role at an important milestone. The company has been renamed 
“ICICI Life Insurance Limited”, strengthening our identity with brand ICICI, that millions 
of Indians associate with trust, strength, and easy access to financial services. 

 
3 
 
As we open this new chapter, our promise of making "Har Kal Aasaan" is firmly rooted 
in our customer-first philosophy. My endeavour will be to further strengthen the 
franchise, accelerate our momentum, and enhance value for all our stakeholders. 
I look forward to working closely with all of you. With that, I hand it over to Amish to take 
you through our business performance. 
 
Amish Banker 
Thank you, Sidharatha. H1-FY2027 was marked by global macroeconomic uncertainty, 
driven by geopolitical tensions. While the Indian economy remained relatively stable, 
risks persisted from supply chain disruptions and elevated inflation. As a result, equity 
markets stayed under pressure, with FIIs continuing to sell. 
Despite this external volatility, we delivered a strong and resilient performance, with VNB 
growing by 22.3% to ₹ 12.83 billion in H1-FY2027, and margins stood at 26.0%. Total 
premium grew by 15.3% year-on-year to ₹ 245.05 billion. New business premium grew 
by 25.0% year-on-year to ₹ 118.21 billion, driven by 10.6% growth in the number of 
policies, reflecting the continued expansion of our customer base. 
Our business model is built on two pillars, protection business, which provides risk 
coverage, and savings business, which creates value through long-term management of 
customer funds.  
In H1-FY2027, our sum assured grew by 30.1% to ₹ 8.81 trillion, supported by a strong 
39.5% year-on-year growth in protection APE. Our sum assured market share stood at 
11.5%. Retail sum assured increased by 34.9% to ₹ 2.32 trillion, driven by robust year-
on-year growth of 47.2% in retail protection. Recently, our flagship term plan, “iProtect 
Smart Plus”, has been awarded “Product of the Year 2026-27” through Nielsen IQ's 
consumer research, a reflection of our commitment to serve innovative and customer-
centric products.  
The overall protection mix increased from 19.3% in H1-FY2026 to 23.4% of APE in H1-
FY2027. Consequently, the savings business mix moderated from 80.7% in H1-FY2026 
to 76.6% in H1-FY2027. 
In the savings business, APE stood at ₹ 37.79 billion in H1-FY2027, registering a growth 
of 9.3% year-on-year. Within savings, annuity segment grew strongly by 50% year-on-
year. Linked business grew by 6.6% year-on-year in H1-FY2027. This segment witnessed 
some softness, especially in the later half of Q2, as uncertain equity markets impacted 
investor sentiment. Our strategy in this segment continues to be on offering wealth 
creation solutions which help navigate market volatility while achieving financial goals 
of the family.  
The non-linked savings business declined by 4.5% year-on-year in H1-FY2027. However, 
this business segment has seen a sharp recovery, with Q2 business being at a similar 
level to last year. Within the non-linked category, non-par mix has increased in Q2 as 

 
4 
 
compared to Q1-FY2027. Group funds business grew by 48% year-on-year in H1-
FY2027. 
Let me now take you through the channel-wise performance.  
Agency channel grew by 3.3% year-on-year in H1-FY2027 to ₹ 11.02 billion. The channel 
is on an improving trajectory, with Q2 growth at 4.1% year-on-year. Direct channel grew 
by 10.9% year-on-year in H1-FY2027 to ₹ 6.79 billion. Together, these channels 
contributed 46.1% to retail business in H1-FY2027. 
As a strategic priority within the agency channel, we continue to optimise product mix, 
which improves profitability and supports sustainable growth. By equipping agents with 
tools and analytics to automate administrative tasks, they can pivot their focus towards 
productive activities. As we go deeper into the micro markets, leverage data analytics 
and technology, we aim to drive higher productivity while ensuring our cost structures 
remain aligned with our evolving business mix. 
In the Direct channel, our focus remains on scaling online business through differentiated 
customer offerings and digital capabilities and deepening our presence in the NRI 
segment through GIFT City. Bancassurance channel grew by 4.6% year-on-year in H1-
FY2027 and contributed 27.4% to APE. 
Partnership Distribution channel grew by 34.1% year-on-year in H1-FY2027 and 
contributed 14.8% to APE. Across both our bancassurance and partnership channels, we 
remain focused on strengthening existing relationships and securing new alliances. Our 
strategy is to build on high-quality business, using mortality and persistency as core 
metrics to ensure long-term sustainable value. 
Group business grew by 39.2% year-on-year in H1-FY2027 and contributed 21.6% to 
APE. Today, we have the strength of 2.41 lakh+ advisors, 52 bank partnerships with 
access to more than 27,000 bank branches, and 1,600+ non-bank partnerships. 
To summarise, our focus will remain on leveraging our core strengths, a customer-centric, 
innovative product portfolio, and a well-diversified distribution architecture enabled by 
strong sales and service capabilities. We will continue to strengthen the proprietary 
channel, execute our micro market strategy, and enhance both depth and breadth in 
multi-partner shops. Combined with our resilient business model, these initiatives will 
enable us to deliver sustainable, long-term growth through varying market conditions. 
I will now hand it over to Dhiren to take you through the regulatory and financial updates. 
 
Dhiren Salian 
Thanks, Amish. Let me start with the regulatory developments. IRDAI has released a 
public consultation paper on recalibrating economics of insurance distribution. This 
paper lays the groundwork for greater efficiency, fostering healthy competition and 
enhanced transparency across the insurance sector. 

 
5 
 
Importantly, it places policyholders at the centre of the reform agenda, aligning the 
insurance sector with the broader national vision of Viksit Bharat. Overall, the paper aims 
to strike a balance between expanding business opportunities and driving greater 
efficiency and productivity across the ecosystem. 
A key element is the recalibration of expenses of management framework, with revised 
limits and a phased glide path to instill stronger cost discipline. As a company, we have 
been on our own efficiency journey over the last few years. We have consistently 
leveraged technology, digital tools, and AI-driven initiatives to improve productivity and 
make our cost structure leaner and better aligned to the evolving product mix. 
Our operating expenses, excluding GST and stamp duty, have reduced at a CAGR of 8% 
over the last three years, an absolute 22% reduction in FY2026 compared to FY2023, 
which reflects the steady and deliberate progress that we have made.  
In the distribution space, the paper proposes an efficiency-oriented approach with 
differentiated commission caps. 
Becoming the most partnerable insurer has been a key strategic priority for us, and we 
will continue to leverage our proprietary ‘Partner Stack’ platform to collaborate closely 
with our partners as these reforms take shape. We view these policyholder-focused 
reforms as a catalyst for growth and long-term value creation for all stakeholders: 
Policyholders, Distributors, and our Company. 
With a strong and resilient business model, we are well positioned to benefit from the 
significant insurance opportunity ahead. As these recalibrations take place, we expect 
the company to emerge even stronger, more policyholder-friendly, more productive, and 
significantly more efficient.  
Now let me get to the financial updates.  
Starting with efficiency metrics, in H1-FY2027, 54% of our savings policies were issued 
on the same day, reflecting the progress we have made in straight-through processing 
and automation. 
Our Cost to Premium ratio, excluding GST, reduced by 30 basis points year-on-year to 
18.3% in H1-FY2027, and the Savings Cost to Premium ratio, excluding GST, reduced by 
90 basis points year-on-year to 11.6% over the same period. This improvement is a direct 
outcome of productivity enhancements and disciplined cost management. 
Our claim settlement ratio remained industry-leading at 99.3% in H1-FY2027, with an 
average turnaround time of 1.1 days for non-investigated claims. Our early claim ratio 
stood at 23%, which is the best-in-class in the industry, highlighting the high quality of 
business we have consistently sourced over the years. 
During H1-FY2027, we settled ₹ 26.27 billion of death claims and paid ₹ 86.34 billion in 
maturity and survival benefits, underscoring our continued commitment to delivering 
timely financial protection and peace of mind to our customers. Customer retention also 
remained healthy, with 13th month persistency at 84.5% in H1-FY2027. 

 
6 
 
Our solvency ratio continues to be strong at 229.9%, and assets under management 
stood at ₹ 3.29 trillion at September 30th, 2026. We continue to maintain a track record 
of not having a single NPA since our inception. ICRA has reaffirmed the rating of our 
existing ₹ 26 billion sub-debt programme as [ICRA] AAA (Stable). Profit after tax grew 
by 26.5% year-on-year to ₹ 7.60 billion in H1-FY2027. 
Our focus is on growing the absolute VNB, which has been demonstrated with the 22.3% 
year-on-year growth in H1-FY2027 to ₹ 12.83 billion. VNB margin stood at 26.0%, an 
expansion of 130 basis points from the full-year margin of 24.7% last year.  
As compared to FY2026, our product mix has moved favorably towards the protection 
business, with sum assured registering a strong growth of 30% year-on-year in half-
year, thereby supporting value creation. Additionally, we kept working towards 
improving the profitability of each line of business through longer tenure of policies, 
higher sum assured multiples, and increasing rider attachment.  
Our embedded value grew by 12.2% year-on-year to ₹ 566.69 billion at September 30th, 
2026. Within the EV, the value of in-force business grew by 12% year-on-year to ₹ 
423.89 billion. 
Thank you, and we're now happy to take any questions that you may have. 
 
Moderator: Thank you very much. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. 
We'll take our first question from the line of Swarnabha Mukherjee from 360 ONE Capital. 
Please go ahead. 
Swarnabha Mukherjee: Hi Sir. Good afternoon and thank you for the opportunity. Three 
questions from my side. First of all, I just wanted to understand the VNB movement. So 
if you could give some colour in terms of both on a year-on-year comparison as well as 
on a quarter-on-quarter comparison that – say year-on-year how much product mix has 
helped the VNB movement vis-a-vis say cost structure, etcetera as well as the yield 
curve, how it has shaped up. And similar for on a quarter-on-quarter basis if you can 
highlight, because I think on the overall protection side, particularly on the group 
protection side on a quarter-on-quarter basis, there was some softness. If you could 
throw some colour on that. 
And also on the cost to total premium number, sir, I think what I observed that when we 
look at the number inclusive of GST, it has gone up, while ex-of-GST the number has 
actually improved. So is there any added element related to the GST changes that has 
kind of gotten factored in this number in this current quarter, if you could highlight that? 
So that would be my first question. 
Second is, sir, wanted some further clarity in terms of the draft regulations. I mean, when 
you are talking to your distributors, and particularly given partnership distribution is one 
of our primary growth engines right now, what are the initial feedbacks you are getting 
in terms of how would the evolving landscape be, what people are thinking in terms of 

 
7 
 
business growth, etcetera if the regulation comes in this shape and form? Some 
comments on this will be very useful. And lastly, if you could give the split between par 
and non-par in the non-linked mix, that would be helpful. That's it from me. 
Dhiren Salian: Thanks, Swarnabha. Let me cover the first question that you placed on 
the VNB margin movement. The right way to look at is from financial year 2026 numbers, 
which we closed the year at a margin of 24.7% and we closed H1 this year at 26%. As 
we had discussed at the Q1 call itself, a large portion of this movement fundamentally is 
the product mix and that continues from quarter one all the way to quarter two as well. 
Not much here. It's just the product mix that is playing out from what's happened through 
this last half-year and you see clearly that the mix is geared more towards protection 
and that is what is helping us deliver the margins at this point. 
You also spoke of cost-to-premium metrics and the reason why we've called out cost-
to-premium ex-GST is because last year, there was no challenge around GST input tax 
credit. If you recall, back in September 2025, that is when the input tax credit challenge 
came about from post the GST changes. While that gave a fillip to retail protection 
growth and to insurance in general, it did create an input tax credit challenge. And so to 
give the reader a perspective of a like-to-like basis, we have called out the GST number 
this time. Of course, as we go through to the end of the year and into next year, we will 
obviously have to look at gross of GST as well. 
Coming to your second question on the consultation paper, I mentioned this in my 
comments as well. I think it's a consultation paper at this point. It's not a draft regulation. 
The regulator has set a time towards the end of this month to collect feedback from all 
stakeholders, including the general public, with the objective that it is customer-centric 
and it is policyholder at its core. And the whole idea being that you're looking at creating 
a foundation which provides for greater efficiency, healthy competition and 
transparency.  
That's been the objective with which this particular paper has been set out. There are a 
set of thoughts that are running within the industry as well. But I think people still have 
to firm it up and provide their inputs to the regulator by the end of the month. So there 
are a lot of conversations. Nothing has come to closure at this point. 
Swarnabha Mukherjee: Yes. If I may ask a follow-up with this. So, I mean, just if I were 
to look at it in terms of how the evolving structure has been in the paper, and even if 
there are some changes, I mean, do you expect that from a manufacturer standpoint that 
in the shorter term there can be a volume impact coming because of the delta in the 
commission structure? 
Dhiren Salian: It's too difficult to call, Swarnabha. The way you also look at this is that 
there is sufficient space that the regulator has set out in terms of renewal commission. 
So in terms of alignment of interest between all three parties, which is the Distributor, 
Customer, and Company, the allowance around renewal commission, which is significant 
at this point, does give us comfort that those entities who are interested in providing 

 
8 
 
value to all stakeholders will continue to distribute. I don't see a challenge around that 
front. 
But like I said, it is too early to take a call. Let us provide our comments. Let the regulator 
put everything together and come up with the draft regulation. They're more than willing 
and you've seen the authority go out of their way to reach out to the general public and 
explain what they're doing. And at the same time, also show that they're willing to take 
in feedback and put their final thoughts together in the form of a draft regulation. So 
we'll have to wait for that to come through, Swarnabha. A little too early to call. 
Swarnabha Mukherjee: Sure, sure. 
Dhiren Salian: Coming to your question on par/non-par, last year, the mix was geared 
more towards par. So this year, for instance, has started to move towards non-par, and 
specifically in the last quarter, the mix is broadly in the range of 60:40, par to non-par. 
Swarnabha Mukherjee: Okay. Understood. Very helpful, Dhiren. Thank you, and all the 
best. 
Dhiren Salian: Thank you. 
Moderator: Thank you. Next question is from the line of Supratim Datta from Jefferies. 
Please go ahead. 
Supratim Datta: Hi. Thanks a lot for the opportunity. My first question is on the 
bancassurance channel. So just wanted to understand that whether the ICICI Bank 
proportion is still around that, you know, 13%-14%? Because what I see is in this channel, 
the growth has been slowing down, and if ICICI Bank proportion is largely similar, then 
that would mean the non-ICICI Bank part is slowing down. Could you help me 
understand that what would be driving that? 
And moving to the agency bit, you know, that has been another channel where despite 
the investments, growth has been soft. Just wanted to understand, how are you looking 
at that channel? What would really help accelerate the growth in this channel? If you 
could give us some colour here, that would be helpful? 
And then moving to the regulation bit, I do understand that it's a draft regulation. But if 
you could give us some understanding around if this paper comes as is, which products 
and which channels would you have to manage the most? Those would be my three 
questions. Thank you. 
Dhiren Salian: Hi, Supratim. So if you look at banca, that grew about 5% in the half-year, 
and roughly half of this banca business is from ICICI Bank, which is broadly stable in the 
range of ₹ 100, 110, 120 crores. So, and which is again focused completely on ULIP and 
protection. 
So in that sense, you have one part of the business, which is broadly steady at the ₹ 100-
120 crores mark, and then you have growth coming in from other channels. So when 
you're looking at the overall, you will still see that average play-through between ICICI 

 
9 
 
Bank versus non-ICICI Bank business. And that's what explains the average growth that 
you see for 5% there. 
Coming to your question on agency, I think if you track the growth of agency across the 
last few quarters, you will see that there's been a fair turnaround from what was the 
deep negative numbers that we had seen in last year to now positive numbers across 
both of these quarters for this current financial year. 
Structurally also, what we have done in agency is to work on the micro market-led 
approach, again with the use of technology, analytics. And structurally, we have also 
ensured that they're looking at products that enhance the business quality, improve 
profitability and provide sustainable growth. So you're seeing the mix also shift within 
the agency business itself. 
So the idea being again endeavor is agency to deliver better growth than company over 
the medium term. And you're starting to see the shift in agency over these last few 
quarters come through at this point. Your third question on the consultation paper, again, 
as I repeated, as I mentioned in the previous answer, it is a consultation paper, very early 
to call. 
I think the regulator is very mindful of what the partners in the ecosystem are or the 
players in the ecosystem are, and is looking at feedback from all participants, including 
the general public. And whatever they produce as the final, or rather the draft regulation, 
will take all of this into account. Thanks. 
Moderator: Thank you. Next question is from the line of Shreya Shivani from Nomura. 
Please go ahead. 
Shreya Shivani: Thank you for the opportunity. I have two questions. First is on the credit 
life business. If you can help us understand, how was the APE growth in this quarter on 
this? And just a follow-up on this, any conversations that we have had with the regulator 
on this product, because that's where the commission cuts have been drastic. 
My second question is on the non-par product. Now we are in a rising rate environment. 
So, as Sidharatha Mishra Sir was mentioning that annuity and protection will be a focus 
area, how much focus will be we putting on non-par products, given it is effectively 
annuity but for younger age group? So, any plans around new product launches, or any 
colour that you can give on that? Thank you. 
Dhiren Salian: Hi, Shreya. So the growth in credit life has been quite in line with what 
you're seeing in the protection growth for this quarter as well. So, it's a fairly decent 
growth that we're seeing at this point. In terms of the regulation -- the consultation 
paper, you're right. It does propose a fairly significant cut, but you see structurally, you 
have to look at credit life from a different perspective. 
See, credit life is, as a protection product, it provides a very important societal need in a 
country. It alleviates the stress of any asset repossession in case of any untimely death 
of the breadwinner. And very specifically, when you look at low-income per capita 

 
10 
 
income groups, where they may not be an asset backing the loan, then the need for credit 
life becomes even more acute to avoid any severe social fallout and also any repayment 
pressure that may come about. 
On top of this, a substantial number of lives are covered by credit life, which currently 
helps furthering the cause of Viksit Bharat. So like I said, this is a consultation paper. The 
regulator is taking feedback from various stakeholders. And we believe that the regulator 
will take these points into account as they put up the draft regulations. Thanks. 
Shreya Shivani: Sure. 
Dhiren Salian: Coming to non-par, so non-par has done quite well in the half-year so far. 
The rates are good. We've also modified some of our offerings to customers to provide 
as best as we can and seeing these numbers come through at this stage. We will 
continue to push on non-par. Again, the whole point is not to force-fit products to 
customers. 
The idea is to understand what are the customer needs and offer these products that are 
relevant for those sets of customers. As you rightly put it, those set of customers who are 
slightly on the younger side who may be looking for guaranteed income products or 
guaranteed return products will find our non-par products quite attractive in their IRRs. 
Shreya Shivani: Right. So, just sorry, I missed the part. Did you already reprice your non-
par product, or you're going to do? What did you mention there? 
Dhiren Salian: So we have repriced. This is a continuous exercise for us. We look at what 
are the yields that are available in market, and then we offer that to customers. It is a 
continuous process, Shreya. 
Shreya Shivani: Got it. Thank you so much. 
Moderator: Thank you. Next question is from the line of Samant Singh from Phillip 
Capital India. Please go ahead. 
Samant Singh: Yes, hi. Good afternoon. Thanks for the opportunity. First, in terms of the 
retail savings, which is like linked portion has grown by six almost seven percentage 
point in this quarter, and non-linked is like flat. Retail savings fell by around 2% in 
September. So what is holding back retail savings? I understand you provided some 
colour on the opening remarks, but if you can give more points to it. And how is October 
trending? So that is the first question. 
Second, coming back to the credit life and the caps, so how much of the credit life 
business comes from ICICI Bank and group companies versus let's say, NBFCs? And is 
the premium that is financed within the loan today? Also, if you can provide that 
attachment rate to home loans, education loans? And the third part to this question is, 
under a 2% cap with no bundling, what volume response can you expect on the credit 
life business? 

 
11 
 
And the third question is on persistency. So 25th month persistency is like 76.2%, which 
is fallen from June, 77%. So which cohorts are driving it, and should we expect a negative 
persistency variance in the FY27 EV walk? So yes, these are the three questions. Thank 
you. 
Dhiren Salian: Hi, Samant. So if you look at the savings, yes, linked sitting at about 7%. 
I think the market volatility, as Amish also pointed out in his comments, has had an 
impact in this quarter. And we will have to wait to see how that plays out, because to 
some degree, the market volatility does impact linked business. 
But within the non-linked business, we have seen a big pick up in the non-participating 
side. And more so, you have seen this pick up on the annuity side, which has grown by 
about 50% in the quarter. 
So effectively, coming back to the way we look at products, it's the question of what the 
customer wants at that point in time that we offer. So between the savings product, we 
are agnostic to the product mix and allow the environment to pick what is relevant for 
the customer there. October too early to call. It's just been about 10-12 days, too early in 
the quarter to call this out. 
Coming to credit life business, we do have a wide diversity of partners within the credit 
life business. A fair share of the business also comes in from the parent bank. We have 
not called out the split between our various partnerships here, but we do have fair degree 
of diversity within the credit life business. 
Your hypothetical question of if the commission rates were to go to 2%, I think we will 
have to wait till we get the draft regulations. It's a little too early to call. Structurally, like 
I mentioned earlier in response to another question, this is fundamentally a protection 
product that serves a very, very societal need. 
And more specifically, when you look at the lower per capita income groups. So I think 
these are some of the points that the regulator will take into account as they firm up the 
draft regulations. 
Your question on 25th month persistency, the same set of challenges that we had seen 
in 13th month last year, they flow through. Essentially, this will move from the 13th to 
the 25th, 25th to the 37th, 37th and then on year after year. So we are not seeing 
anything unusual there. This is in some way expected. 
Samant Singh: Thanks and all the best. 
Dhiren Salian: Thanks. 
Moderator: Thank you. Next question is from the line of Tejas D'Cunha from Aditya Birla 
Capital. Please go ahead. 
Tejas D'Cunha: Yes. So this would be a follow-up question to the credit life questions 
that we have seen earlier. And with the regulator intent of prohibiting bundling, it is likely 
to boost the group term life product. And even the regulator has mentioned that group 

 
12 
 
term life can be sold as a bundled, an alternative to credit life business. So my question 
is, what is the current contribution of group term life to the protection business? 
And with this intent that we have seen, how will it benefit products from ICICI Bank into 
getting more business into the group term life portfolio? 
Dhiren Salian: So, Tejas, just to tackle that point on bundling, see, all our products are 
sold with the consent from customers. And customers are given a choice of how to fund 
the premium. And we believe that with all of our distribution partners, which is the banks 
and NBFCs, they follow a very transparent process in making this clear to the customer. 
Having said that, again, this is a consultation paper. We are going through the details. 
The regulator is picking up feedback, and they will come up with their draft regulations.
